successors.name: Spanish Empire
successors.text: the Sulu archipelago, which the sultan and his datus submitted to Spain in the capitulation signed at Jolo on 22 July 1878 ('Bases of Peace and Capitulation')

ledger.x: c. 1457: Sharif ul-Hashim founds the Sulu sultanate at Buansa. Infobox 'Established c. 1457' (reign 1457-1480); the article says 'either on 17 November 1405 or 1457'. Bruneian vassal until 1578.
Archipelago grows from Jolo to Tawi-Tawi and Basilan in Cliopatria's 1529 shape.
1704: Sulu receives north-eastern Borneo from Brunei.
1705: Sulu gives up Palawan to Spain.
1789: Bulungan becomes a vassal of Sulu.
1855: Bulungan stops paying tribute to Sulu.
22 January 1878: the Sultan of Sulu signs the concession over North Borneo to Overbeck and Dent.
ledger.cp: British North Borneo Company (Overbeck and Dent)

ledger.x: July 1878: Spain's occupation of Jolo becomes sovereignty over the archipelago by the 'treaty of the Sultan of Jolo and his datus submitting to Spain, signed at Licup (Jolo) July 22, 1878'.
22 July 1878: the sultan gives up sovereignty to Spain.

wars.name: Spanish-Moro conflict
wars.outcome: Spain landed at Jolo in 1637, sent a punitive expedition in 1731, took Jolo in 1850-1851 and again in 1876; the sultan accepted peace in 1737 and 1836, signed the treaty of 19 April 1851 and the capitulation of 22 July 1878.

wars.name: Bruneian Civil War of 1660
wars.outcome: Muhyiddin won; Sulu claims eastern Sabah as its reward, a claim the page calls disputed and does not date.

certainty.note: An island sultanate with a sphere along the Borneo coast; no survey line is dated by the pages opened.
The North Borneo concession (22 January 1878) and the capitulation (22 July 1878) are dated deeds.
